titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §§80–86: The Thicket, the Cangue, Sorqan-Shira
about: Seven sections, one escape. §80 is Temüjin's hiding in the thicket (the saddle that slips, the rock that blocks the way, the starving, the cutting-out) and his capture by the Taichi'ud. §81 is the Red Circle day: the feast on the Onan, the blow to the weak guard, the flight into the river with the cangue floated off. §§82–83 are the Taichi'ud's search by moonlight and Sorqan-Shira's speeches, in which he finds Temüjin lying in the water, says nothing, and steers the searchers away. §§84–85 are Temüjin's decision to trust Sorqan-Shira's house, the sign of the churning, the sons Chimbai and Chila'un who burn the cangue, and the wool cart. §86 is the search of the house and the hot-wool trick. The grammar to watch is the converb chain (-žu / -ču / -ġed, Ming 着, 'having … -ing') and the speech-closing keġen / keġežü; the conditional converbs (-ġesü, -basu, Ming 呵); the reflexive-possessive (-ban / -jan / -jen / -jüġen, 'one's own'); the reciprocal -ldu- ('together'); and the instrumental forms mör(i)-er-en and mör(i)-jer. The hard places, flagged in the notes, are the sentence ending in tein ele naitaγdan in §82, the nama-ji tangle at the end of §83, the sparrow proverb with turimtai in §85, and who 'had him put away' in §85.

sentences.t: Temüžin šiγui dotora γurban qonožu γarsu keġen
sentences.l: Temüžin, dense-wood inside, three spending-the-night, "I-go-out" saying,
sentences.i: Temüjin, having spent three nights inside the thicket, said, "I will go out,"
sentences.n: §80 opens a chain of converbs (-žu / -žü / -ču, Ming 着, 'having … -ing') that I cut into units at the natural joints; each note says where the chain runs. Here the scene is the thicket (šiγui, Ming 密林) where Temüžin is hiding from the Taichi'ud, and qonožu is qono- 'spend the night' (stem inferred from Ming 宿着) + -žu. γarsu is Ming 出去我, 'let me go out': the -su ending is a wish or intention, and the Ming reads it as first person. keġen (麽道) is the converb of keġe- 'say' that closes a quotation, so the quotation is "I will go out."

morph.gloss: Temüjin, a boy's name (Ming (兒)名) [(兒)名]
to spend the night (stem inferred) [宿着]
wish / intention: let me … (Ming 我; form uncertain)
converb: -ing, closing a quotation (Ming 麽道)

sentences.t: mori-jan kötölžü aisuqui-dur morin-ača emeġel in-ü mültürežü qosorčuγ̇u.
sentences.l: his-own-horse leading-along, coming when, horse-from saddle his slipping-off, fell.
sentences.i: As he came, leading his horse along, his saddle slipped off the horse and fell.
sentences.n: mori-jan is morin 'horse' + the reflexive-possessive -jan (Ming 自的行), 'his own horse', here without a case ending; kötölžü is kötöl- 'lead along' + -žü. aisuqui-dur is aisu- 'come' + the participle -qui + -dur: 'at the coming', so 'when he came' (Ming 來時). morin-ača is the ablative 'from the horse'. emeġel 'saddle' (鞍子) and in-ü 'his' (the genitive, placed after the noun it owns) follow. mültürežü qosorčuγu (脫着墮落了) pairs a converb 'slipping off' with the past 'fell' (qosorčuγu, probably -γu with -č-; the exact shape is uncertain). Shiratori's full stop closes this sentence.

morph.gloss: dative-locative: at the time of (Ming 時)
his, her (third-person genitive, placed after its noun) [他的]
to slip off, come away (Ming 脫) [脫着]
to fall off, drop (Ming 墮落了; stem inferred) [墮落了]

sentences.t: Qarižu üžeġesü emeġel kömüldürgelegseġer olaṅlaγsaγ̇ar mültürežü qosorčuγ̇u.
sentences.l: Turning-back when-he-looked, saddle, breast-strap-as-it-was-fastened, girth-as-it-was-fastened, slipping-off, fell.
sentences.i: Turning back, when he looked, the saddle had slipped off and fallen, with breast-strap and girth still buckled.
sentences.n: Qarižu is qari- 'turn back' + -žu. üžeġesü is üže- 'see' + the conditional converb -ġesü: 'when (he) looked' (Ming 看呵). Then two odd words: kömüldürgelegseġer (Ming 扳胷依舊扣着) and olaṅlaγsaγar (肚帶依舊扣着). Each is a noun (kömüldürge 'breast-strap', olaṅ 'girth') + a verb-maker -le- 'fasten' + the participle -γsan + an ending -ar/-er (the instrumental): 'in the state of having been fastened'. The Ming 依舊 'as before' supports this; the exact shape of the ending is my reading. The scene is odd and the point is the surprise: the straps were still done up and the saddle came off anyway.

morph.gloss: to turn back (Ming 囘著) [囘著︀]
breast-strap, the strap across the horse's chest (Ming 扳胷) [扳胷 依舊扣着]
instrumental: in the state of (Ming 依舊, 'as before'; form uncertain)
girth, belly-band (Ming 肚帶) [肚帶依舊扣着]
instrumental: in the state of (Ming 依舊; form uncertain)
to slip off, come away (Ming 脫) [脫着]
to fall off, drop (Ming 墮落了) [墮落了]

sentences.t: Olaṅ či boltuγai.
sentences.l: Girth, you, let-it-be.
sentences.i: "The girth too, let it be;
sentences.n: A hard line. Shiratori prints it with a full stop and no quotation marks. Olaṅ is 'girth'; či is 'you' (the Ming gives 也, 'also', not 你, so či may be a particle here, not the pronoun; i reads it as 'too'). boltuγai is bol- 'become, be' + the optative -tuγai ('let it be', Ming 可 'it is allowed'). My reading is that Temüžin is grumbling that the girth might give way but the breast-strap should not; this is a guess, and the Ming gives only 'girth, also, permissible'.

morph.gloss: you, or a particle (Ming 也 'also'; uncertain) [也]
optative: let it be, may it (Ming 可)

sentences.t: Kömüldürge basa ker mültürekü büleġe.
sentences.l: Breast-strap again how slipping-off was.
sentences.i: how did the breast-strap slip off as well?"
sentences.n: Kömüldürge 'breast-strap' (扳胷) is the subject; basa 'again, also' (再); ker 'how' (怎生); mültürekü 'slipping-off' is the participle -kü (Ming 脫落的), and büleġe is the past of bü- 'be' (有來). So 'how was (it) slipping off?' The question is rhetorical: nothing explains the failure of the straps, and Temüžin is reading it as a sign, as the next line shows.

morph.gloss: how, in what manner (Ming 怎生) [怎生]

sentences.t: Teṅgeri idqan aqu-ju" keġežü
sentences.l: Heaven forbidding, can-it-be,
sentences.i: "Could Heaven be forbidding (me)?" he said,
sentences.n: Teṅgeri is 'Heaven' (天) and idqan is Ming 止當, 'restrain, forbid'. aqu-ju is aqu- 'be' (a form of a- 'be' with a -qu participle) + -ju, Ming 莫不, 'can it be that…?', the tag that turns a statement into a question of suspicion. I read the line as "Could Heaven be holding (me) back?" The Ming leaves the object unstated. keġežü 'saying' closes the quotation.

morph.gloss: to restrain, hold back (Ming 止當; stem inferred) [止當]
question tag: can it be …? (Ming 莫不; form uncertain)

sentences.t: qarižu basa γurban qonoba.
sentences.l: turning-back again three spent.
sentences.i: and turned back and spent three more nights.
sentences.n: qarižu 'turning back' (囘著) + basa 'again' + γurban 'three' + qonoba (宿了), qono- 'spend the night' + the past -ba. The chain ends here in a finite verb. So that is three nights, then three more, six in all; a third three follows after the rock (next units), which brings the total to nine, the jesün qonoγ 'nine nights' of the unit after.

sentences.t: Basa γarču aisuqui-dur šiγui-jin amasar-a qošiliγ-un tedüi čaγan gürü amasar-a böglen unažuγ̇u.
sentences.l: Again going-out, coming when, thicket's mouth-at, tent so-big white stone, mouth-at blocking, fell.
sentences.i: Again he went out, and as he came to the mouth of the thicket, a white rock as big as a tent had fallen and blocked the entrance.
sentences.n: Basa γarču 'again going out' (出着), aisuqui-dur 'when coming' as before. šiγui-jin is the genitive 'of the thicket' (-jin after a vowel, Ming 的); amasar-a is amasar 'mouth, entrance' + the dative -a (Ming 行). qošiliγ-un tedüi is 'tent-of so-much', the size comparison: 'as big as a tent' (Ming 帳房的那般, 'tent-like'); čaγan gürü is 'white rock'. böglen is Ming 塞着, 'blocking', a converb from a stem like bögle- (the form is uncertain); unažuγu is una- 'fall' + the past ending -žuγu (倒了), 'had fallen down'. The entrance is blocked by a rock fallen across it.

morph.gloss: dative-locative: at the time of (Ming 時)
genitive: of (after a vowel; Ming 的)
mouth, entrance (Ming 口子) [口子 行]
tent, round tent (Ming 帳房) [帳房 的]
so much, as big as (after a genitive: size comparison; Ming 那般) [那般]
mouth, entrance (Ming 口子) [口子 行]
to block, plug (Ming 塞着; stem inferred) [塞着]

sentences.t: "Teṅgeri idqan aqu-ju" keġežü qarižü basa γurban qonoba.
sentences.l: "Heaven forbidding can-it-be," saying, turning-back again three spent.
sentences.i: "Could Heaven be forbidding (me)?" he said, and turned back and spent three nights more.
sentences.n: The same words as before, now in a second turn: Teṅgeri idqan aqu-ju keġežü, then qarižü (the front-vowel spelling of the converb of qari- 'turn back') basa γurban qonoba. Shiratori ends this stretch with a full stop after qonoba. Count so far: three, three, three nights.

morph.gloss: to restrain, hold back (Ming 止當) [止當]
question tag: can it be …? (Ming 莫不; form uncertain)
to turn back (Ming 囘著) [囘著︀]

sentences.t: Basa jesün qonoγ ideġen ügei ažu nere ügei ker üküdeküi;
sentences.l: Again nine nights food without, staying, name without how dying;
sentences.i: Again he stayed nine nights without food. "How am I to die with no name?
sentences.n: Basa jesün qonoγ is 'again nine night(s)' (九宿); ideġen ügei is 'food, a meal' + ügei 'without' (茶飯無), so 'no food'; ažu is a- 'be, stay' + -žu (住着). nere ügei is 'name without' (名無): a man with no name. ker üküdeküi (怎生死的) is 'how dying', with üküdeküi the participle -küi of üküde- 'die'; Shiratori's semicolon follows it. Shiratori puts no quotation marks here; I read the clause as Temüžin's thought, which the next unit closes with 'I will go out'. The count is puzzling (three, three, three, and now 'again nine'); it may be a total, and I leave it as printed.

morph.gloss: food, a meal (Ming 茶飯) [茶飯︀]
to be, stay (Ming 住着) [住着]

sentences.t: γarsu keġežü
sentences.l: I-go-out saying,
sentences.i: I will go out!" he said,
sentences.n: γarsu keġežü again: 'let me go out, saying'. The quotation that began at nere ügei closes here. (Compare the first γarsu keġen at the head of the section.)

sentences.t: tere amasar böglen umaγsan qošiliγ-un tedüi čaγan gürü horčin γarγ̇asu ülü bolqu
sentences.l: That mouth blocking fallen tent so-big white stone, around going-out if, not possible,
sentences.i: If he went out round the white rock, as big as a tent, that had fallen and blocked the entrance, it was not possible;
sentences.n: A clause in two halves. tere amasar böglen umaγsan qošiliγ-un tedüi čaγan gürü is a relative phrase: 'that white rock, as big as a tent, blocking the entrance, having fallen', where umaγsan (Ming 倒了的) is the participle -γsan, 'that has fallen' (the spelling umaγ- beside the earlier una- is Shiratori's, not mine). horčin is Ming 周圍, 'around' (uncertain whether a noun or a postposition). γarγasu is γar- 'go out' + -γasu, the conditional (出呵), 'if / when (he) went out'. ülü bolqu is 'not' + the participle of bol- 'be': 'it will not be possible, not feasible'.

morph.gloss: to block, plug (Ming 塞着) [塞着]
past participle: that has … (Ming 倒了的)
tent, round tent (Ming 帳房) [帳房 的]
so much, as big as (Ming 那般) [那般]
around, round about (Ming 周圍) [周圍]

sentences.t: mudud-i sumuči kituγai-jar(i)-jan hoγtoriγ̇ad mori-jan qaltariγ̇uluγ̇ad γarqui-luγ̇a
sentences.l: Woods (acc.), arrow-shaver, knife-with his-own cutting-through, his-own-horse making-slip-through, as-he-went-out,
sentences.i: With his own arrow-shaving knife he cut through the timber, and as he slipped his horse through and came out,
sentences.n: mudud-i is mudud 'trees, timber' (Ming 木每, a plural) + the accusative -i, 'the wood (acc.)'. sumuči is 'arrow-shaver, a man who dresses arrows' (削箭的); kituγai-jar(i)-jan is a knife (kituγai, 刀) + an ending -jar/-iyar (the instrumental, 'with') + the reflexive -jan, 'with his own knife'. The Ming glosses the middle part 自的 (敎). hoγtoriγad (割斷了) is 'cutting through' (hoγtor- + -γad, converb); qaltariγuluγad is a causative converb of qaltari- 'slip, slide' (滑擦着), 'making (the horse) slide through'. γarqui-luγa is γar- 'go out' + the participle -qui + -luγa, which the Ming glosses 呵, 'when, as'. Whether -luγa means 'as' or 'though' is not certain; the Taichi'ud's watching follows in the next unit.

morph.gloss: trees, timber (plural of mod; Ming 木每) [木每行]
agent-maker: a maker of … (arrow-shaver; Ming 削箭的)
knife (Ming 刀兒) [刀兒 自的 (敎)]
to cut through, sever (Ming 割斷了) [割斷了]
to slip, slide (Ming 滑擦着) [滑擦着]
to go out [出去了 呵]

sentences.t: Taičiγ̇ud sakižu ažuγ̇u.
sentences.l: Taičiγud guarding was.
sentences.i: the Taichi'ud were keeping watch.
sentences.n: Taičiγud is the clan name (Ming 種名), sakižu is saki- 'guard' + -žu (守着) and ažuγu is a- 'be' with the past -γu, 'was'. So 'were guarding (him)'. The converb + a- 'be' make a continuous past, 'was …-ing'.

morph.gloss: the Taichi'ud, a clan name (Ming 種名) [種名]

sentences.t: Barižu abču odba.
sentences.l: Seizing, taking, went-off.
sentences.i: They seized him, took him, and went off.
sentences.n: barižu bari- 'seize' + -žu (拿着), abču ab- 'take' + -ču (將着), odba od- 'go' + -ba, past. This is a short new chain, closed by the full stop (the last unit ended in a finite verb). Who 'they' are is plain from context.

morph.gloss: to seize, grasp (Ming 拿着) [拿着]

sentences.t: Temüžin-i Tarγutai-Kiriltuγ abču odču
sentences.l: Temüžin (acc.), Tarγutai-Kiriltuγ taking, going,
sentences.i: Tarqutai-Kiriltuq took Temüjin away,
sentences.n: A new §. Temüžin-i has the accusative -i (Ming 行) 'Temüžin (object)'. Tarγutai-Kiriltuγ is one man's name (Ming 人名): Shiratori joins the two parts with a hyphen; I give it as one name. abču 'taking' and odču 'going' (去着) are converbs, 'taking, going', so 'taking (him) away'. The chain continues, and I cut it into short units to keep the story readable.

morph.gloss: Temüjin, a boy's name (Ming (兒)名) [(兒)名 行]
Tarqutai-Kiriltuq, a man's name (Ming 人名) [人名]

sentences.t: ulus irgen -dür(i)-jen žasaγlažu
sentences.l: Realm, people to-his-own, rule-making,
sentences.i: laying down a rule for his own realm and people,
sentences.n: ulus (國) 'realm' and irgen (百姓) 'people' are a pair, 'the realm and its folk'. The ending is split off by Shiratori and printed on the next line of the edition as -dür(i)-jen: dative-locative -dür + (i) + the reflexive -jen, 'to his own'. Ming 自的行. žasaγlažu is žasaγ 'law, order' + the verb-maker -la- + -žu: 'making a rule', so here 'giving an order'. I read it as Tarqutai ordering his people to take turns holding the prisoner; the Ming 法度做着 is 'making a regulation', and the next unit tells what the regulation was.

morph.gloss: people, common folk (Ming 百姓) [百姓]
law, order (Ming 法度) [法度做着]

sentences.t: ail-dur nigen qonoγ̇ulun qonoγ̇ulun bitüġülün
sentences.l: Camp-in one lodging-causing, lodging-causing, taking-around,
sentences.i: and had him lodge one night in each camp, passing him from camp to camp,
sentences.n: ail-dur is ail 'camp, household' + -dur (Ming 每營裏, 'in each camp'); nigen 'one' (一). qonoγulun is qono- 'spend the night' + the causative -γul- + the converb -n, 'causing to lodge' (Ming 敎宿); it is doubled, qonoγulun qonoγulun, for the repeated action, and bitüġülün is Ming 徇着, 'taking round, parading': I read a stem bitü- (its sense uncertain; 'close' does not obviously fit) + the causative -ġül- + -n. The sense: a regulation that each camp take him for one night in turn.

morph.gloss: camp, encampment (Ming 每營) [每營 裏]
to take around, parade (Ming 徇着; stem uncertain) [徇着]

sentences.t: jabuqui-dur žun-u teriġün sara-jin harban žirγoγ̇an-a hulaγ̇an tergel üdür
sentences.l: Walking when, summer's first month's sixteenth-on, red circle day,
sentences.i: and while they went about in this way, on the sixteenth of the first month of summer, the day called the Red Circle,
sentences.n: jabuqui-dur is jabu- 'walk, go about' + -qui + -dur, 'when going' (Ming 行的時). žun-u is the genitive of žun 'summer', teriġün 'head, first' (頭), sara-jin 'of the month', harban žirγoγan-a 'sixteen' (harban 'ten' + žirγoγan 'six' + the dative -a, Ming 六行; the dative is the date marker, 'on the sixteenth'). hulaγan tergel üdür: 'red circle day' (紅圖兒日). The Ming glosses tergel '(圖)兒' with a character in parentheses, so the word is uncertain; I give 'circle' as a guess from the Ming and flag it.

morph.gloss: to walk, go about [行的 時]
dative-locative: at the time of (Ming 時)
genitive: of (after a vowel; Ming 的)

sentences.t: Taičiγ̇ud Onan-(n)u ergi deġere qurimlaldužu naran šingeġesü tarqaba.
sentences.l: Taičiγud, Onan's bank on, feasting-together, sun setting if, dispersed.
sentences.i: the Taichi'ud held a feast together on the bank of the Onan, and when the sun set they dispersed.
sentences.n: Taičiγud (種名) again the subject; Onan-(n)u is the genitive of the river name (the (n) is Shiratori's marker that the n belongs to the case ending: the stem Onan ends in n); ergi 'bank' (岸), deġere 'on, above' (上, a postposition-like noun). qurimlaldužu: qurim 'feast, banquet' (筵會) + the verb-maker -la- + the reciprocal -ldu- + -žu, 'feasting together' (相筵會着). naran 'sun' (日); šingeġesü is Ming 落了呵, 'if / when (it) set' (the stem šinge- is my guess; conditional -ġesü). tarqaba is tarqa- 'scatter' + -ba, 'dispersed'. Shiratori's full stop is after tarqaba.

morph.gloss: the Taichi'ud, a clan name (Ming 種名) [種名]
the river Onan (Ming 河名) [河名 的]
feast, banquet (Ming 筵會) [相筵會 着]
to set, sink (Ming 落了; stem inferred) [落了呵]

sentences.t: Temüžin-i tere qurim-dur gelbüre köġün küġün abčiražü büleġe.
sentences.l: Temüžin (acc.), that feast-at, weak lad person taking-along was.
sentences.i: At that feast a weak young fellow was taking Temüjin along,
sentences.n: Temüžin-i is again the object. tere qurim-dur 'at that feast' (筵會裏). gelbüre is Ming 弱, 'weak, feeble'; köġün (子) 'son, lad' and küġün (人) 'person' stand side by side, so 'a weak boy-fellow', or 'a weak lad of a man'; I treat köġün küġün as a pair. abčiražü büleġe is Ming 將着有來, 'was taking along': abčira- is ab- 'take' + the compound -čira- (the form is not clear to me) + -žü, with büleġe 'was' as before. So: 'a weak lad was taking him along', that is, the guard.

morph.gloss: Temüjin, a boy's name (Ming (兒)名 行) [(兒)名 行]
feast, banquet (Ming 筵會) [筵會 裏]
to take along, have in hand (Ming 將着; form uncertain) [將着]

sentences.t: Qurim-un haran-i tarqaγ̇ulun tere gelbüre köġün-eče buγaγ̇u tatažu abču
sentences.l: Feast's people (acc.) causing-to-disperse, that weak lad-from cangue pulling, taking,
sentences.i: When the people of the feast had been sent off, he seized the cangue from that weak lad,
sentences.n: Qurim-un is the genitive 'of the feast', haran-i is haran (the common folk, 'the black people', 人每) + the accusative; tarqaγulun is tarqa- 'scatter' + the causative -γul- + -n, 'causing to disperse'. In Ming 敎散了, 'had them dispersed'. The causative -γul- needs someone who sends them off, and the sentence does not name him. köġün-eče is köġün + the ablative -eče, 'from the lad' (Ming 幼小人行); buγaγu is the cangue (枷), tatažu 'pulling' (扯着), abču 'taking' (要着, 'getting'). The subject, unwritten, is Temüžin. So: 'took the cangue away from the weak lad by pulling'. A -ču chain.

morph.gloss: common people, the black people (Ming 人每) [人每行]
to pull, drag (Ming 扯着) [扯着]
to take, get (Ming 要着) [要着]

sentences.t: heki in-ü nigente deledüġed güjižü
sentences.l: Nape his one-blow striking, running,
sentences.i: struck him once on the back of the neck, ran,
sentences.n: heki is Ming 頭項, 'nape, neck'; in-ü 'his' follows its noun. nigente is nigen 'one' + the case ending -te (Ming 一下, 'one blow'), 'at one (stroke)'. deledüġed is Ming 打了, 'having struck' (stem deledü- is my reading; the converb -ġed). güjižü is güji- 'run' + -žü (走着). This is the swift part of the chain: strike and run.

morph.gloss: nape, back of the neck (Ming 頭項) [頭項]
his, her (third-person genitive, placed after its noun) [他的]
to strike (Ming 打了; stem inferred) [打了]

sentences.t: Onan-(n)u tün dotora kebteġesü üžegdekü keġežü
sentences.l: Onan's wood inside lying-down if, being-seen, saying,
sentences.i: saying, "If I lie down inside the wood of the Onan, I shall be seen,"
sentences.n: Onan-(n)u tün dotora is 'the Onan's forest inside' (斡難訥林內). kebteġesü is kebte- 'lie down' + the conditional -ġesü (Ming 臥着呵), 'if (I) lie'. üžegdekü is üže- 'see' + the passive -gde- + the participle -kü: 'being seen' (被着見), 'it will be seen'. keġežü 'saying' ends the quotation. Only the Ming gives me the 'I'; the verbs carry no person.

morph.gloss: the river Onan (Ming 河名) [河名 的]

sentences.t: usun-u qarki -dür gedergü kebtežü
sentences.l: Water's channel-in, face-up lying,
sentences.i: he lay on his back in the channel of the water,
sentences.n: usun-u is the genitive 'of the water' (水的); qarki is Ming 溜道, 'a channel, a watercourse'; -dür 'in'. The edition prints -dür as the next line's start. gedergü is Ming 仰, 'face up, on the back'; kebtežü is kebte- 'lie down' + -žü (臥着).

morph.gloss: face up, on the back (Ming 仰) [仰]
to lie down (Ming 臥着) [臥着]

sentences.t: buγaγ̇u-ban usun huruγ̇u urusγan niγ̇ur ile kebtebe.
sentences.l: Cangue his-own water with-the-flow flowing, face open lay.
sentences.i: let the cangue float off with the flow of the water, and lay with his face bare.
sentences.n: buγaγu-ban is the cangue with the reflexive -ban (Ming 自的行), 'his own cangue'; usun 'water' (水), huruγu 'down with, with the current' (順), urusγan is the converb of urus- 'flow' + -γan (Ming 流着). So 'his own cangue flowing with the water': he sets the cangue afloat. niγur ile kebtebe: niγur 'face' (面), ile 'openly, bare' (露着), kebtebe 'lay down' (臥了). The subject of 'flowing' is the cangue, not Temüžin, I read -γan as a causative -γa- + the converb -n ('letting flow'), which would explain why it is not -žu, but the Ming 流着 does not mark a causative (敎), so this is uncertain.

morph.gloss: cangue, wooden collar (Ming 枷) [枷 自的行]
along with, with the current (Ming 順) [順]
converb -n, perhaps with a causative -γa-: 'letting flow' (form uncertain)

sentences.t: Tere aldaγsan küġün jeke daγ̇u-bar "barija küġün aldaba" keġen qailaqui-dur
sentences.l: That escaped person, great voice-with, "seize person escaped," saying, calling when,
sentences.i: The man who had let him slip away shouted at the top of his voice, "Seize him! The man has escaped!" and when he called,
sentences.n: A new §, and a hard first line. Tere aldaγsan küġün is 'that escaped person' (Ming 那脫了的人): aldaγsan is alda- 'slip away, lose' + -γsan, 'who has slipped away'. The shouter must be the weak guard, so I take aldaγsan as 'who let (him) escape'; but the Ming reads it as 'escaped person' and the same phrase also names the fugitive in the next line, so it is not certain which. jeke daγu-bar is 'great voice-with' (also in Ming 大聲敎), the instrumental -bar. barija is bari- 'seize' + -ja (shaped like the 'let us' ending -je of bedereje, but the Ming 拿住 has no 咱 'us', so I read it as a call, 'seize!'; the ending is uncertain). aldaba is the past 'has escaped' (脫了也). keġen closes the quotation; qailaqui-dur is qaila- 'call out' + -qui + -dur 'when calling' (叫的時).

morph.gloss: to slip away, lose (Ming 脫) [脫了的]
past participle: that has … (Ming 了的)
instrumental: with, by means of (Ming 敎)
ending of a call: seize! (shape of the 'let us' ending -je; Ming 住; form uncertain)
converb: -ing, closing a quotation (Ming 麽道)
to call out (Ming 叫) [叫的 時]
dative-locative: at the time of (Ming 時)

sentences.t: tarqaγsad Taičiγ̇ud qurižu irežü üdür metü saraγ̇ur-a Onan-(n)u tün-(n)i bederebe.
sentences.l: Dispersed Taičiγud, gathering, coming, daylight like moonlight-in, Onan's forest (acc.) searched.
sentences.i: the Taichi'ud, who had scattered, gathered and came, and by moonlight, bright as day, they searched the forest of the Onan.
sentences.n: tarqaγsad is tarqa- 'scatter' + -γsad, the plural past participle (Ming 散了的每), 'those who had dispersed'. qurižu irežü is 'gathering, coming': quri- 'gather' + -žu, ire- 'come' + -žu. üdür metü is 'day-like' (白日般), metü 'like' after a noun; saraγur-a is saraγur 'moonlight' (撒剌兀剌, 月明) + the dative -a (行), 'in the moonlight'. Onan-(n)u tün-(n)i 'the Onan's forest (acc.)', and bederebe, Ming 排尋了, 'searched in a line'; the stem bedere- is my reading. Shiratori's full stop closes it.

morph.gloss: past participle, plural: those who have … (Ming 散了的每)
the Taichi'ud, a clan name (Ming 種名) [種名]
the river Onan (Ming 河名) [(河)名 的]
to search through, search in a line (Ming 排尋了; stem inferred) [排尋了]

sentences.t: Qarki-dur kebtežü büküi-ji Süldüsün Sorγan-Šira žöb daγ̇arižu üžežü ügülerün:
sentences.l: Channel-in lying one (acc.), Süldüsün Sorγan-Šira, exactly passing-by, seeing, speaking-while:
sentences.i: Sorqan-Shira of the Suldus, passing close by, saw the man lying in the channel and said:
sentences.n: Qarki-dur 'in the channel' (溜道裏); kebtežü büküi-ji is 'lying + the one who is' (臥着有的行): büküi is the participle of bü- 'be' and the ending -ji marks the accusative (Ming 行), so 'the one who lies'. Süldüsün is the clan name (種名, the Suldus), Sorγan-Šira is the man's name (人名); I follow Shiratori's hyphen and give the name as one. žöb is Ming 正, 'exactly, just'; daγarižu is Ming 經過着, 'passing by' (from daγari-); üžežü is üže- 'see' + -žü (見着); ügülerün is ügüle- 'speak' + -rün, 'speaking, and then', the time-converb that introduces a speech (the colon is Shiratori's).

morph.gloss: channel, watercourse (Ming 溜道) [溜道 裏]
to lie down (Ming 臥着) [臥着]
participle: the one who … (Ming 有的)
the Suldus, a clan name (Ming 種名) [種名]
Sorqan-Shira, a man's name (Ming 人名) [人名]
to pass by (Ming 經過) [經過]

sentences.t: "Žöb ele eimü arγatu-jin tula nidün-dür(i)-jen γaltu niγ̇ur-tur(i)-jan geretü keġen
sentences.l: "Just so: such talent-having's because-of, eyes-in his-own fire-having, face-in his-own light-having," saying,
sentences.i: "Just so: because he is so gifted — 'fire in his eyes, light in his face,' they say —
sentences.n: Žöb ele eimü is 'exactly, only, thus' (Ming 正但這般). arγatu-jin tula is 'because of the one with arγa': arγa is skill, talent (Ming 才有的; the stem is my guess), -tu the possessive 'having', -jin the genitive, and tula (上頭) 'because of, on account of'. nidün-dür(i)-jen is nidün 'eye' + -dür 'in' + (i) + -jen 'one's own' (自的行): 'in his own eyes'; γaltu 'fire-having' (火有的) is γal 'fire' + the possessive -tu; niγur-tur(i)-jan 'in his own face' and geretü 'light-having' (光有的) the same way. keġen 'saying' closes this stretch; who is saying it the words do not tell, and the 'they say' of i is my guess. The speech goes on in the next unit. This is a hard sentence; I follow the Ming order.

morph.gloss: skill, talent (Ming 才有; stem uncertain) [才有(的) 的]
because of, on account of (Ming 上頭) [上頭]
converb: -ing, closing a quotation (Ming 麽道)

sentences.t: Taičiγ̇ud aqa deġü-deġen tein ele naitaγdan ažuγ̇u.
sentences.l: Taičiγud, elder-brothers younger-brothers-their-own thus indeed envying were.
sentences.i: the Taichi'ud have been envious of their own kin.
sentences.n: A line I cannot fully fix. The Ming runs 種名兄弟自的行那般但嫉妒有: the Taichi'ud, elder-brothers and younger-brothers (aqa deġü) with the reflexive -deġen (自的行, 'their own'), tein 'thus, in that way' (那般), ele 'indeed', naitaγdan 'envying' (naitaγda- + converb -n), ažuγu 'were' (有來). I take aqa deġü-deġen (Ming 弟 自的行, with 行 marking the object) as the ones envied, 'their own kin'; Temüžin is surely the kinsman meant, but the words do not name him. The quotation of Sorγan-Šira's speech runs on to bi in the next unit.

morph.gloss: the Taichi'ud, a clan name (Ming 種名) [種名]
younger brother (Ming 弟) [弟 自的行]
thus, in that way (Ming 那般) [那般]
to be envious (Ming 嫉妒; stem inferred) [嫉妒]

sentences.t: Či tein kü kebte; ülü žaγ̇aqu bi" kēġed nögčibe.
sentences.l: You thus indeed lie; not telling I, saying, passed-on.
sentences.i: You, lie there as you are; I shall not tell." So saying, he went on his way.
sentences.n: Či is 'you' (赤, 你), tein 'thus' (那般), kü an emphatic particle (只, 'just, indeed'), and kebte is the imperative of kebte- 'lie' (the Ming has 臥着, 'lying'), so 'you, lie just so'. ülü žaγaqu bi is 'not (ülü) announcing (žaγa- 'tell' + the participle -qu) I (bi)' (不吿我): the participle plus bi serves as a future, 'I shall not tell'. kēġed is keġe- 'say' + the converb -ġed (the long ē is Shiratori's) and nögčibe is nögči- 'pass on, go beyond' + -be (過去了). A short speech.

morph.gloss: thus, in that way (Ming 那般) [那般]
to lie down (the bare stem serves as the imperative here; form uncertain) [臥着]
to pass on, go past (Ming 過去了) [過去了]

sentences.t: Basa qarin bedereje keġeldüküi-dür Sorγan-Šira ügülerün:
sentences.l: Again returning "let-us-search" (their) saying-together-when, Sorγan-Šira speaking-while:
sentences.i: "Let us turn back and search again," they said together, and Sorqan-Shira said:
sentences.n: Basa qarin bedereje is 'again back let-us-search': qarin 'back, again' (囘), bedereje is bedere- + the first-person wish -je ('let us'; the Ming glosses this word 排尋 only, and adds 咱 to the same ending in the next sentence). keġeldüküi-dür is keġe- 'say' + the reciprocal -ldü- + -küi-dür 'when …-ing', so 'when they said together' (Ming 其說時). The speakers are the searchers. Then Sorγan-Šira speaks again, ügülerün as above.

morph.gloss: to search through (Ming 排尋) [排尋]
'let us' (first-person wish; the Ming 咱 stands on the same ending in the next sentence, not here)
dative-locative: at the time of (Ming 時)
Sorqan-Shira, a man's name (Ming 人名) [人名]

sentences.t: "Mün mün mör(i)-er-en ese üžegsen γažar(i)-jan üžeġed qarin bedereje"
sentences.l: "The-very the-very way-by not seen (of) land-his-own having-looked, back let-us-search,"
sentences.i: "Let us go back the very same way, look over the ground we have not yet seen, and search again,"
sentences.n: Mün mün (本本) is 'the very, the same', doubled for stress; mör(i)-er-en is mör 'track, road' + (i) + -er (the instrumental 'by') + -en (the reflexive 'own'), 'along our own way' (Ming 路自的行). ese üžegsen is 'not-yet seen' (不曾見的): ese is the negative of the past (not ülü), üžegsen is üže- 'see' + -gsen. γažar(i)-jan is γažar 'land, place' (地) + (i) + -jan; üžeġed is 'having looked' (看了). I read: 'by the very same way, having looked at the places not yet seen, back let us search' (the sense in the Ming is that they re-walk the road and look at the unvisited spots). The tie between 'same road' and 'unseen ground' is odd and I cannot tell if the Ming glossators had a different idea. Shiratori ends the sentence with keġebe on the next unit.

morph.gloss: the very, the same (Ming 本) [本]
the very, the same (Ming 本) [本]
track, road (Ming 路) [路 自的行]
not (negative of the past; Ming 不曾) [不曾]
past participle: that has been … (Ming 見的)
land, place (Ming 地) [地 自的行]

sentences.t: keġebe. "Že-kü" keġeldübe.
sentences.l: said. "So-be-it," said-together.
sentences.i: So he spoke. "So be it," they agreed.
sentences.n: keġebe is keġe- 'say' + -ba/-be (說了). Že-kü is Ming 那般者, 'so be it, very well', two particles (že + kü); keġeldübe is the reciprocal past, 'said together, agreed' (共說了).

morph.gloss: so be it, very well (Ming 者) [那般者︀]
emphatic particle, as in tein kü above (the Ming 那般者 glosses the pair)

sentences.t: Mün mün mör(i)-jer qarin bederežü basa Sorγan-Šira daγ̇arižu ügülerün:
sentences.l: The-very the-very way-by back searching, again Sorγan-Šira passing-by, speaking-while:
sentences.i: They went back by the same road, searching, and Sorqan-Shira again passed by and said:
sentences.n: mör(i)-jer is mör + (i) + -jer, the instrumental (Ming 路行); this is the same ending as -jar in kituγai-jar(i)-jan above, in its front-vowel form. bederežü 'searching', again a converb, then basa 'again', Sorγan-Šira, daγarižu 'passing by' and ügülerün 'speaking'. I read the ending of this unit as the start of a new quotation, whose words follow.

morph.gloss: the very, the same (Ming 本) [本]
the very, the same (Ming 本) [本]
to search through (Ming 排尋着) [排尋着]
Sorqan-Shira, a man's name (Ming 人名) [人名]
to pass by (Ming 經過着) [經過着]

sentences.t: "Aqa deġü čin-u ama-γ̇an šidu-ban bileġüden aisu. Tein kebte qadaγ̇uži-kü" kēġed nögčibe.
sentences.l: "Elder-brothers, younger-brothers, your mouth-your-own, teeth-your-own grinding coming. Thus lie, be-careful," said-and passed-on.
sentences.i: "Brothers, you come grinding your mouths and teeth. Lie there as you are and take care." Having said it, he went on.
sentences.n: The hardest speech of §82, and I am unsure of the first half. Aqa deġü is 'elder, younger brother', a form of address to the Taichi'ud ('brothers'); čin-u is the genitive of či, 'your' (你的); ama-γan is 'mouth' + -γan, the reflexive after a vowel; šidu-ban is 'tooth' + -ban (牙自的行). bileġüden is bile- 'whet, grind' + the converb (磨着), aisu 'come' (來有; the stem shows no ending, and I read it as a present, 'are coming', from the Ming 有). So: 'brothers, your mouth, teeth grinding, you come', but whether this is a joke about their loud eagerness, a warning of their noise, or something said for Temüžin to hear, I cannot tell. Then Tein kebte 'lie so' and qadaγuži-kü, Ming 謹慎, 'be careful' (qadaγuži- + the ending -kü), a hint to the one in the water. kēġed nögčibe 'having said, passed on' as before.

morph.gloss: reflexive-possessive: one's own (after a vowel; Ming 自的行)
to whet, grind (Ming 磨着; form uncertain) [磨着]
thus, in that way (Ming 那般) [那般]
to lie down (Ming 臥着) [臥着]
to be careful, take care (Ming 謹慎) [謹︀愼]
to pass on, go past [過去了]

sentences.t: Basa "qarin bedereje" keġeldüküi-dür Sorγan-Šira basa ügülerün:
sentences.l: Again "back let-us-search," (their) saying-together-when, Sorγan-Šira again speaking-while:
sentences.i: Again, as they said together, "Let us turn back and search," Sorqan-Shira spoke once more:
sentences.n: A new §, and it repeats the shape of §82: a search party, a verdict, Sorγan-Šira's speech. The Ming 再 'again' glosses basa twice. The line is a copy of the earlier ones: qarin bedereje (the first-person wish -je, 'let us') keġeldüküi-dür 'when they said together'.

morph.gloss: to search through (Ming 排尋) [排尋]
dative-locative: at the time of (Ming 其說時)
Sorqan-Shira, a man's name (Ming 人名) [人名]

sentences.t: "Taičiγ̇ud köġüd ta gegeġen čaγaγ̇an üdür gübčin küġü aldaba.
sentences.l: "Taičiγud lords, you bright white day whole person escaped.
sentences.i: "You lords of the Taichi'ud, in broad white daylight a whole man has slipped away!
sentences.n: köġüd is the plural of köġün 'son'; but the Ming glosses it 大王每, 'great lords, princes', and l and i follow the Ming: 'lords of the Taichi'ud'. ta is 'you (plural, polite)' (您). gegeġen čaγaγan üdür is 'bright (gegeġen, 明), white (čaγaγan, 白), day': in full daylight. gübčin küġü: gübčin (全) 'whole, entire' + küġü 'person' (人): 'a whole man', which may mean an able-bodied man; the Ming leaves it at 全人. aldaba 'has escaped'. The 'in broad daylight' is the reproach: they let him go while they could see.

morph.gloss: the Taichi'ud, a clan name (Ming 種名) [種名]
son, here 'lord, prince' (Ming 大王每, which reads the plural as an honorific address) [大王(每)]

sentences.t: Edöġe qaraṅγui süni ker olqun.
sentences.l: Now black night how get-shall?
sentences.i: Now, in the dark of the night, how are we to find him?
sentences.n: Edöġe 'now' (今), qaraṅγui 'dark, black' (黑), süni 'night' (夜), ker 'how' (怎生), olqun is ol- 'find, get' + the participle -qun (得), the future / question participle. (Bida 'we', 咱, belongs to the next sentence.) The ending -qun makes a question and marks no person; 'we' in i is the searchers' own, as the next sentence's Bida shows.

morph.gloss: how, in what manner (Ming 怎生) [怎生]

sentences.t: Bida basa mün mün mör(i)-jer ese üžegsen γažar(i)-jan üžeġed qarin bedereġed tarqažu
sentences.l: We again the-very the-very way-by not seen (of) land-his-own having-looked, back having-searched, dispersing,
sentences.i: Let us again go by the same road, look over the ground we have not yet seen, search back, and then disperse,
sentences.n: Bida 'we' (咱) opens the sentence (Shiratori's capital). Then basa mün mün mör(i)-jer ese üžegsen γažar(i)-jan üžeġed qarin bedereġed tarqažu: this repeats §82's 'same road, not-yet-seen ground' phrase word for word, so the same doubts apply. I read bedereġed as 'having searched' (排尋, converb -ġed). tarqažu is 'scattering' (散着).

morph.gloss: we, including the one spoken to (Ming 咱) [咱]
the very, the same (Ming 本) [本]
the very, the same (Ming 本) [本]
not (negative of the past; Ming 不曾) [不曾]
past participle: that has been … (Ming 見的)
land, place (Ming 地) [地 自的行]
to search through (Ming 排尋) [排尋]
to scatter, disperse (Ming 散着) [散着]

sentences.t: manaγar üdür čiγ̇ulžu erije. Qaγ̇a odqu tere buγaγ̇utu küġün"
sentences.l: tomorrow day gathering let-us-seek. Where going-to that cangue-having person?"
sentences.i: and gather tomorrow and look for him. Where will that man in the cangue go?"
sentences.n: manaγar is Ming 明 'tomorrow, the morrow' with üdür 'day' (明日 as one gloss), čiγulžu is 'gathering' (čiγul- 'gather' + -žu), and erije is eri- 'seek' + the first-person wish -je (咱尋). Qaγa 'where' (那裏) + odqu (od- 'go' + -qu, the future participle, 去的), so 'where will he go?'. tere buγaγutu küġün is 'that cangue-having man' (the possessive -tu, 'having a cangue', Ming 枷有的). A reasoned argument: a man with a cangue can't get far.

morph.gloss: tomorrow, the next day (Ming 明) [明]
to gather, assemble (Ming 聚着) [聚着]
where, which way (Ming 那裏) [那裏]

sentences.t: keġebe "Že-kü" keġeldüžü qarin bederežü
sentences.l: said. "So-be-it," saying-together, back searching,
sentences.i: he said. "So be it," they agreed, and searched back,
sentences.n: keġebe 'said' (說了), Že-kü 'so be it' as before, keġeldüžü is the reciprocal 'saying together' + -žü (共說着), qarin bederežü 'back searching'. The sentence goes on with Sorγan-Šira's speech.

morph.gloss: so be it, very well (Ming 者) [那般者︀]
to search through (Ming 排尋着) [排尋着]

sentences.t: Sorγan-Šira basa daγ̇arižu ügülerün: "Edüi bedereġed qarižu manaγar erije keġeldübe.
sentences.l: Sorγan-Šira again passing-by speaking-while: "This-much having-searched, turning-back tomorrow let-us-seek," (we) said-together.
sentences.i: and Sorqan-Shira again passed by and said: "So much for the searching; let us turn back and look tomorrow, so we have agreed.
sentences.n: The order here is the Ming's: Sorγan-Šira basa daγarižu ügülerün. Edüi is Ming 只這般, 'only this much, so much and no more', bedereġed 'having searched', qarižu 'turning back', manaγar erije 'tomorrow let us seek', keġeldübe 'said together' (共說了) marks no person; since the speech is Sorγan-Šira's, I read it as 'we have agreed', the searchers and himself; Shiratori's quotation mark opens at Edüi and does not close until the end of §83, so this is all one speech.

morph.gloss: Sorqan-Shira, a man's name (Ming 人名) [人名]
to pass by (Ming 經過着) [經過着]
only so much, thus far (Ming 只這般) [只這般]
to search through (Ming 排尋了) [排尋了]
to turn back (Ming 囘著) [囘著︀]
tomorrow, the next day (Ming 明日) [明日]

sentences.t: Edöġe man-i tarqaγ̇ulun baražu eke-ben deġü-ner(i)-jen erin od.
sentences.l: "Now us causing-to-disperse, finishing, mother-your-own, younger-brothers-your-own seeking go.
sentences.i: Now, when we have all been sent away, go and look for your mother and your brothers.
sentences.n: The speech is still Sorγan-Šira's, but he now speaks to Temüžin, though nothing in the text says so; I read it from what he says. sentences.l: Me (acc.) saw, saying, person-by if-seen, was-seen, saying, do not say," said-and passed-on.
sentences.i: If you are seen by anyone, do not say, 'He saw me.' Do not say, 'I was seen.'" So he spoke, and went on his way.
sentences.n: Nama-ji is nama (the oblique stem of bi 'I') + -ji (accusative), 'me' (我行); užebe is 'saw' (見了). keġen closes a quotation (麽道). küġün-e is 'to a person' (人行); üžegdeġesü is the passive-conditional 'if (one) is seen' (被見呵); üžegdebe 'was seen' (被見來), keġen again, bu kelele 'do not say' (休說): bu is the prohibition, kelele the imperative of kele- 'speak'. I do not trust my reading of this tangle. Nama-ji 'me' is whoever speaks the inner words, so the sense may be: if anyone sees you, do not say 'he saw me' (naming Sorγan-Šira) nor 'I was seen', a request for silence that fits Temüjin's thought in §84 that Sorqan-Shira saw him and told no one. sentences.l: Sorγan-Šira: "This again such hot wool inside how bearing?"
sentences.i: Sorqan-Shira: "This too — in such hot wool, how is one to bear it?"
sentences.n: The sentence has been running without a main verb since unit 62; here Sorγan-Šira speaks. ene 'this' (這), basa 'again', eimü 'such, thus' (這般); qalaγun-a is qalaγun 'hot' + the dative -a (熱行); noṅγasun dotora 'wool inside' (毛內); ker 'how'; daγusqu is Ming 當的, 'bearing, enduring' (daγus- with the participle -qu; the stem is uncertain). Read with the context, the question means that no one could bear it inside wool so hot; the next unit has the searcher leave.

sentences.t: kēġesü nünčiġülsün baγ̇užu jorčiba.
sentences.l: saying-when, the-searcher coming-down went-off.
sentences.i: When he had said this, the searcher climbed down and went away.
sentences.n: kēġesü is keġe- 'say' + the conditional -sü, 'when (he) said' (說呵). nünčiġülsün is Ming 搜的, 'the one who searches, a searcher' (nüṅči- + an agent ending -ġülsün, perhaps the causative -ġül- + -sun; uncertain), baγužu is baγu- 'come down' + -žu (下來着), and jorčiba, jorči- 'go off' + -ba (去了). Shiratori's full stop closes §86, and the part ends with the searchers gone.
